messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: P1 GPU capacity exhaustion - eu-west-1. Elevated 429s on /v1/generate and /v1/chat. Queue depth per hotpath > 4.5k; hotpool saturation. Autoscaler attempted scale but hit max_instances. Runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-hotpool-saturation>

jamie (oncall): ack. I'm jumping in. any obvious recent deploys?

maria (sre): seeing a spike starting ~2267887000. Related change earlier today to rate-tier assignment in dispatch: 'tier_assignment_v2' rollout at 2267800000 — but rollout status shows green.

ashish (infra): not me — there was a config tweak to tokenbucket defaults for dedicated customers this morning (lowered burst to 3x -> 2x). I'll check the PR.

olivia (eng-runtime): logs show a bunch of `429: rate_limited` coming from hotpath queues. stacktrace snippets: ```
2026-04-12T10:12:21Z ERROR dispatch rate_limiter: token_bucket_refill: window_millis=1000 tokens=0 client_id=dedicated-54321
2026-04-12T10:12:21Z WARN  request_queue: enqueue latency=2200ms qlen=4720 route=/v1/generate model=gpt-8x
```

jamie (oncall): customers impacted?

product-support: customer-reports: - AcmeGames: ~60% 429s for player chat endpoints since 10:12. - DataQ: bulk-embedding jobs delayed; some failures. Both are on dedicated/premium tiers.

rohit (dedicated): confirmed. Dedicated pools reporting pool_error_rate + queue_backlog. Some dedicated pools hit node limits (soft cap 12 nodes). autoscaler logs: ```
[autoscaler] scale_attempt: desired=18 actual=12 max_cap=12 reason=hard_cap
[autoscaler] cooldown: last_scale=2267880000 cooldown_remaining=600s
```

maria (sre): hypothesis: token-bucket + tier policy change reduced effective throughput for dedicated hotpool, while traffic pattern had a sudden short spike of small generates -> high RPS. That drove queue growth; autoscaler wanted to scale but hit configured max_instances; cooldown prevented immediate further scaling.

jamie (oncall): plan of attack: 1) short-term mitigation: temporarily raise max_instances for affected dedicated pools and relax cooldown; bump tokenbucket refill rate for tier 'dedicated' to avoid immediate 429s. 2) mid-term: rollback tier assignment change if we confirm misapply. 3) notify customers and update status. Who can apply the pool cap change now?

ashish (infra): I can apply the cap change but need an approval. Suggest patching pool config: ```
# patch hotpool config
hotpool.max_instances: 24
hotpool.scale_cooldown_s: 60
rate_limits.tiers.dedicated.token_refill_per_sec: 2000
```

jamie (oncall): do it. jamie -> go for it, +maria for verification. tag ops-bot so we get audit.

ashish (infra): applying now. `kubectl patch configmap hotpool-config -n inference --patch '{"data":{"max_instances":"24","scale_cooldown":"60"}}'`

ops-bot: Change deployed by ashish (infra) at 2026-04-12T10:19:45Z. AuditID: a1b2c3.

maria (sre): verifying metrics... graphs show queue depth dropping from 4720 -> 800 over 90s. 429 rate trending down.

olivia (eng-runtime): token refill bump applied. Also noticed that tier routing has a fallback policy that currently favors 'global' token bucket when local bucket exhausted — that combined with aggressive bucket minburst caused many HEAD-of-line 429s. I'm going to temporarily enable passthrough fallback to let requests land on non-burstlimited pools: `dispatch.fallback.mode=passthrough`

ops-bot: dispatch config updated by olivia (eng-runtime) at 2026-04-12T10:20:52Z. AuditID: d4e5f6.

jamie (oncall): update to customers? product-support can you start status page note: target "degraded performance" for eu-west-1, dedicated customers; ETA for mitigation ~15m.

product-support: posting status update now. Will DM major accounts (AcmeGames, DataQ) with mitigation steps.

olivia (eng-runtime): quick note: we found an edge in the tokenbucket code where `token_refill_rate` gets rounded down for large tenant IDs due to int32 cast in shared limiter. Fix PR ready but not deploying mid-incident. Link: <https://redwood.internal/pulls/5809>

jamie (oncall): good catch. not deploying now. keep as post-incident fix. For now changes look effective?

maria (sre): yes — 429 spike reduced from 48% -> 3% in 8 minutes. CPU/GPU saturation for hotpool reduced; autoscaler no longer blocked.

rohit (dedicated): re-checking dedicated SLA risk: we've avoided large customer failures but some tail requests still see 429s at 1-2%. acceptable for now. We'll follow up with config PR to remove the tokenbucket rounding bug.

ashish (infra): I reverted the tokenbucket burst change partially — restored burst multiplier to 3x for dedicated in a targeted manner. Logged change in infra-changes channel.

jamie (oncall): putting this thread into a short incident report. Please add notes: root cause candidate = combined rollout of tier-assignment and tokenbucket default change that reduced effective burst capacity + autoscaler cap + cooldown prevented scaling during spike. Immediate mitigations = increased max_instances, reduced cooldown, raised token_refill, enabled passthrough fallback.

product-support: Status update posted: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-04-12/eu-west-1-gpu-saturation — customers notified.

maria (sre): next actions (post-incident): - revert / audit tier-assignment rollout targeting. - ship PR to fix int32 cast in limiter. - add an autoscaler safety to allow emergency override when queue depth > X. - add a synthetic smoke test for dedicated tier token_refill. Assign owners?

olivia (eng-runtime): I'll own the limiter fix PR and smoke test.

ashish (infra): I'll own autoscaler emergency override change.

rohit (dedicated): I'll run a customer-impact postmortem with AcmeGames + DataQ contacts and share notes.

jamie (oncall): thanks everyone. closing incident thread once 24h of stable metrics. leaving follow-ups in #postmortems. :thumbsup:
